name: Spotify
verdict_reason: Navidrome is a lovely server for music you own — and Spotify's product is music you don't. Self-hosting replaces the player, not the catalog, and the catalog is the subscription.
what_you_lose: The catalog: everything you haven't bought — which for most subscribers is everything
Discovery — Discover Weekly has no self-hosted answer, because the input is everyone else's listening
Zero-effort availability on every speaker, car and TV that ships a Spotify button

what_broke: Nothing — Navidrome is a single container that boots in seconds. The economics even pass our rubric. The capability gap is the entire verdict: it can only play files you bring.

notes: If you already own a serious music library (rips, Bandcamp), flip this to a personal YES — Navidrome + the Subsonic app ecosystem is genuinely better than Spotify for owned music. Our verdict answers the question most subscribers are asking.
